SANCTIONS

Article 11
(1) The Regional Government facilitates the establishment of women's protection institutions.
(2) The Regent establishes policies, programs and activities for women's protection to eliminate all forms of discrimination and acts of violence against women in the Region.
(3) The implementation of policies, programs and activities for women's protection as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out by establishing, developing, strengthening or utilizing task forces, forums, working groups or other institutions.
(4) The membership of task forces, forums, working groups or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (3) shall consist of relevant Regional Work Units, community leaders, religious leaders, and universities.
(5) Further provisions regarding the establishment of task forces, forums, working groups or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Central Bangka Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Central Bangka.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Central Bangka Regency.
5. Gender is a concept that refers to roles and responsibilities as women and as men that are created and internalized in the family, society and community culture where we live including expectations, attitudes, characteristics, behavior of how to be a man and how to be a woman.
6. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
7. Women's empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social capabilities, knowledge and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
8. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
9. Violence is any act against the law, with or without using means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
10. Disability is an individual who has physical or mental limitations.
11. Regional cooperation is an agreement between governor and governor or governor and regent/mayor or between regent/mayor and other regent/mayor, and or governor, regent/mayor with third parties, which is made in writing and creates rights and obligations.

CHAPTER VI
COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 14
(1) The community can participate in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection.
(2) Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, groups or social community organizations.
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may take the form of:
a. active role in policy formulation;
b. cooperation; and/or
c. complaints/reports.
(4) The procedures for community participation as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

1.5.rationale: In the original Indonesian text, “kekerasan” is defined narrowly in Pasal 1 angka 9 as unlawful acts against physical/psychological integrity causing danger to life/body or deprivation of liberty (“terhadap fisik dan psikis… bahaya bagi nyawa, badan… terampasnya kemerdekaan”). The regulation discusses protection from violence generally (Pasal 8, Pasal 17) and women’s economic/work rights (Pasal 5(1)(d),(g); Pasal 9), but it does not classify economic abuse/exploitation/neglect as a form of violence. Because the document does not explicitly cover “economic violence” as a violence type, the judge’s ‘No’ is consistent with the text; the golden ‘Yes’ appears to be an over-interpretation.

5.3.evaluator_rationale: While the policy mentions cooperation with various institutions and includes community and religious leaders, none of the provided sentences explicitly reference traditional/cultural organizations or traditional/cultural leaders.

Pasal 15(2) adds: “Dalam hal Daerah mendapatkan bantuan pendanaan… dari Pemerintah…”—i.e., if the region receives funding assistance from the (central) Government, it must be implemented per laws.
